title: Clinical Practice Guidelines by the IDSA, AAN, and ACR: 2020 Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis and Treatment of Lyme Disease
key_findings: Recommends 28-day oral antibiotics for Lyme arthritis, IV ceftriaxone or a second oral course for partial responders, and DMARDs/synovectomy (not more antibiotics) for antibiotic-refractory arthritis, which it frames as post-infectious.
relevance_notes: The governing mainstream treatment standard for Lyme arthritis.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Lyme Arthritis
journal_or_publisher: Infectious Disease Clinics of North America
key_findings: Reviews clinical picture (knee-predominant large-joint swelling, strong IgG seropositivity), diagnostics, and the antibiotic-responsive vs antibiotic-refractory distinction.
relevance_notes: Authoritative mainstream clinical review of the topic.

title: Antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis is associated with HLA-DR molecules that bind a Borrelia burgdorferi peptide
key_findings: ~79% of antibiotic-refractory patients carry an OspA-peptide-binding HLA-DR allele vs ~46% of responsive patients, implicating HLA-restricted autoimmunity in refractory disease.
relevance_notes: Genetic-susceptibility cornerstone of the infection-induced-autoimmunity model.

title: A novel human autoantigen, endothelial cell growth factor, is a target of T and B cell responses in patients with Lyme disease
key_findings: Identifies endothelial cell growth factor (ECGF) as the first human autoantigen targeted by T and B cells in Lyme disease, especially antibiotic-refractory arthritis.
relevance_notes: First molecular evidence of autoimmunity in human Lyme arthritis.

title: Antibodies to Endothelial Cell Growth Factor and Obliterative Microvascular Lesions in the Synovium of Patients With Antibiotic-Refractory Lyme Arthritis
key_findings: Anti-ECGF antibody responses correlate with obliterative microvascular lesions in refractory synovium, linking the autoimmune response to vascular pathology.
relevance_notes: Connects autoantigen response to histologic damage.

title: Annexin A2 is a target of autoimmune T and B cell responses associated with synovial fibroblast proliferation in patients with antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis
key_findings: Annexin A2 is a second identified autoantigen, with responses tied to synovial fibroblast proliferation in refractory arthritis.
relevance_notes: Extends the autoantigen panel beyond ECGF.

title: Autoimmunity to synovial extracellular matrix proteins in patients with postinfectious Lyme arthritis
key_findings: Identifies T and B cell autoimmunity to synovial extracellular-matrix proteins (e.g., fibronectin-1, laminin) in postinfectious Lyme arthritis.
relevance_notes: Broadens the autoimmune target set and reinforces the post-infectious model.

title: Spirochete antigens persist near cartilage after murine Lyme borreliosis therapy
key_findings: Intravital microscopy shows B. burgdorferi antigen deposits persisting near cartilage after antibiotics clear live organisms, offering a non-infectious mechanism for refractory arthritis.
relevance_notes: Keystone of the 'persistent antigen, not persistent infection' position.

title: Borrelia burgdorferi peptidoglycan is a persistent antigen in patients with Lyme arthritis
key_findings: Detects B. burgdorferi peptidoglycan in synovial fluid of Lyme arthritis patients; the cell-wall fragment is a slowly-cleared, inflammation-driving retained antigen.
relevance_notes: Provides a concrete human antigen explaining post-treatment inflammation.

title: Evidence assessments and guideline recommendations in Lyme disease: the clinical management of known tick bites, erythema migrans rashes and persistent disease
key_findings: ILADS GRADE analysis rates retreatment evidence very low quality and favors individualized care, including optional extended antibiotics with shared decision-making.
relevance_notes: Primary minority/ILADS treatment-guideline position.

title: Chronic Lyme Disease: An Evidence-Based Definition by the ILADS Working Group
key_findings: Proposes a formal ILADS definition of chronic Lyme disease grounded in persistence claims.
relevance_notes: Frames the minority diagnostic category underlying extended-treatment practice.

title: Lyme arthritis: an epidemic of oligoarticular arthritis in children and adults in three Connecticut communities
key_findings: Original description of the Lyme, Connecticut arthritis cluster that defined the disease.
relevance_notes: Foundational/historical anchor for the entire field.

title: Lyme disease
key_findings: Classic review establishing the natural history including late arthritis in ~60% of untreated patients.
relevance_notes: Canonical clinical reference for natural history.

title: Two controlled trials of antibiotic treatment in patients with persistent symptoms and a history of Lyme disease
key_findings: Randomized trials found no durable benefit of prolonged antibiotics for persistent post-Lyme symptoms.
relevance_notes: Key evidence cited by mainstream bodies against extended antibiotics.

title: The clinical assessment, treatment, and prevention of Lyme disease, human granulocytic anaplasmosis, and babesiosis: IDSA clinical practice guidelines
key_findings: Prior IDSA guideline; superseded by the 2020 IDSA/AAN/ACR guideline but historically central to the controversy.
relevance_notes: Historical baseline for treatment standards and the ILADS/IDSA dispute.

title: Borrelia Burgdorferi (StatPearls)
key_findings: Reference overview of B. burgdorferi microbiology, transmission, and disease including arthritis.
relevance_notes: Background reference for the spirochete and clinical features.

title: Lyme arthritis: linking infection, inflammation and autoimmunity
key_findings: Synthesizes the two-phase (infectious then post-infectious autoimmune) model of Lyme arthritis.
relevance_notes: Most current mainstream synthesis of pathogenesis.

title: Persistence of Borrelia burgdorferi in Rhesus Macaques following Antibiotic Treatment of Disseminated Infection
key_findings: Recovered residual B. burgdorferi by xenodiagnosis/PCR in macaques after antibiotic therapy of disseminated infection.
relevance_notes: Primate evidence cited by the persistence camp; organisms appear attenuated/non-cultivable.

title: Persistence of Borrelia burgdorferi following antibiotic treatment in mice
key_findings: Detected antibiotic-tolerant, largely non-cultivable spirochetes persisting in mice by xenodiagnosis and PCR after ceftriaxone.
relevance_notes: Murine persistence evidence; interpretation (viable vs residual) is contested.

title: Drug Combinations against Borrelia burgdorferi Persisters In Vitro: Eradication Achieved by Using Daptomycin, Cefoperazone and Doxycycline
key_findings: Identifies in-vitro persister subpopulations and a three-drug combination that eradicates them in culture.
relevance_notes: In-vitro basis for combination/pulse antibiotic proposals; not validated clinically.

title: Characterization of Biofilm Formation by Borrelia burgdorferi In Vitro
key_findings: Reports B. burgdorferi biofilm formation in vitro with EPS matrix, a recognized antimicrobial-tolerance mechanism.
relevance_notes: Microbiology basis for biofilm-persistence claims; downstream clinical claims outrun the data.

title: Detection of Borrelia burgdorferi DNA by polymerase chain reaction in synovial fluid from patients with Lyme arthritis
key_findings: B. burgdorferi DNA detectable in synovial fluid before treatment and generally cleared after; basis for both 'residual DNA' and 'persistence' readings.
relevance_notes: The shared data point that both camps cite.

title: A critical appraisal of 'chronic Lyme disease'
key_findings: Landmark appraisal distinguishing documented Lyme and post-treatment symptoms from the loosely-defined 'chronic Lyme disease' label, warning it is often applied without evidence of infection and masks alternative diagnoses.
relevance_notes: The defining mainstream statement separating the contested 'chronic Lyme' label from recognized entities.

title: Chronic Lyme disease: a review
journal_or_publisher: Infectious Disease Clinics of North America
key_findings: Reviews the terminology and evidence, distinguishing post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (real, ~10-20% of treated patients) from unsubstantiated chronic-infection claims.
relevance_notes: Authoritative review establishing the PTLDS-vs-chronic-Lyme distinction.

title: 2020 IDSA/AAN/ACR Lyme Disease Guidelines (persistent symptoms / retreatment sections)
key_findings: Recommends against prolonged or repeated antibiotics for persistent symptoms after treated Lyme; supports symptom-directed care.
relevance_notes: Governing mainstream standard on chronic/persistent Lyme management.

title: Two controlled trials of antibiotic treatment in patients with persistent symptoms and a history of Lyme disease
key_findings: Randomized trials found no durable benefit of prolonged antibiotics for persistent post-Lyme symptoms.
relevance_notes: Core evidence against long-term antibiotics for chronic Lyme.

title: Posttreatment Lyme disease syndrome
journal_or_publisher: Infectious Disease Clinics of North America
key_findings: Characterizes PTLDS as a real syndrome of persistent fatigue, pain, and cognitive symptoms after treated Lyme, with unresolved post-infectious pathophysiology.
relevance_notes: Mainstream framing of PTLDS as real but not active infection.

title: Association of Persistent Symptoms after Lyme Neuroborreliosis and Increased Levels of Interferon-alpha in Blood
key_findings: Found elevated interferon-alpha in blood of patients with persistent symptoms after Lyme neuroborreliosis, suggesting a measurable immune correlate.
relevance_notes: Objective biological correlate for persistent post-Lyme symptoms (mainstream).

title: Association of small fiber neuropathy and post treatment Lyme disease syndrome
key_findings: Documents objective small-fiber neuropathy in a subset of PTLDS patients, evidence of real nerve pathology.
relevance_notes: Objective finding countering the 'purely psychological' view of PTLDS.

title: Chronic Lyme Disease: An Evidence-Based Definition by the ILADS Working Group
key_findings: Proposes a formal ILADS definition of chronic Lyme disease grounded in persistence claims and individualized treatment.
relevance_notes: Primary minority definition of the contested entity.

title: Persistence of Borrelia burgdorferi in Rhesus Macaques following Antibiotic Treatment of Disseminated Infection
key_findings: Recovered residual B. burgdorferi after antibiotic therapy in primates, cited to support post-treatment persistence.
relevance_notes: Best animal evidence for persistence; human/clinical implication contested.

title: Reassessing Chronic Lyme Disease and Post-Treatment Lyme Disease Syndrome as Focal Infections
key_findings: Proposes reframing chronic Lyme/PTLDS as residual focal infection in privileged sites.
relevance_notes: Recent hypothesis-level reframing; not established.

title: Empirical validation of the Horowitz Multiple Systemic Infectious Disease Syndrome Questionnaire for suspected Lyme disease
key_findings: Operationalizes the MSIDS multi-infection model that folds chronic Lyme into a multi-system framework.
relevance_notes: Minority diagnostic framework frequently used to define chronic Lyme.

title: How Lyme Disease Spreads / Transmission (CDC)
authors: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
journal_or_publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
key_findings: States Lyme is transmitted by the bite of infected blacklegged ticks; no credible evidence of sexual transmission, person-to-person spread, or transmission via breast milk; the spirochete's biology is incompatible with sexual transmission.
relevance_notes: Authoritative mainstream statement of transmission routes.

title: Maternal-fetal transmission of the Lyme disease spirochete, Borrelia burgdorferi
key_findings: First documented maternal-fetal transmission: after untreated first-trimester maternal Lyme, spirochetes were found in fetal liver, spleen, bone marrow, heart, brain, and kidney at autopsy.
relevance_notes: Foundational evidence that B. burgdorferi can cross the placenta.

title: A systematic review on the impact of gestational Lyme disease in humans on the fetus and newborn
key_findings: Systematic review: adverse outcomes are associated mainly with untreated maternal Lyme; evidence is limited and confounded; no consistent congenital malformation syndrome proven; prompt treatment reduces risk.
relevance_notes: Best mainstream synthesis of gestational Lyme evidence.

title: Maternal Lyme borreliosis and pregnancy outcome
key_findings: Observational study reporting more adverse pregnancy outcomes in maternal Lyme, particularly when untreated or inadequately treated.
relevance_notes: Observational signal for vertical-transmission harm; confounded, minority-weighted.

title: Evidence review for person-to-person transmission (NICE Lyme disease guideline NG95)
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
key_findings: Systematic review found insufficient evidence for person-to-person transmission (sexual or congenital as a defined syndrome); 'congenital Lyme disease' was subsequently removed from ICD-11.
relevance_notes: Basis for the mainstream position that a congenital Lyme syndrome and sexual transmission are not established.

title: Culture and identification of Borrelia spirochetes in human vaginal and seminal secretions
key_findings: Reports culturing/detecting Borrelia in human semen and vaginal secretions, including in partner couples, argued as evidence for possible sexual transmission.
relevance_notes: Primary sexual-transmission detection claim; single-group, contamination-vulnerable, unreplicated.

title: Sexual transmission of Lyme disease: challenging the tickborne disease paradigm
key_findings: Commentary arguing detection of Borrelia in genital secretions challenges the tick-only transmission paradigm.
relevance_notes: Minority commentary advancing the sexual-transmission hypothesis.

title: Congenital Syphilis (StatPearls)
key_findings: Congenital syphilis is a fully established disease: the spirochete Treponema pallidum is transmitted transplacentally (and sexually), causing defined fetal/neonatal disease.
relevance_notes: Anchors the congenital-syphilis analogy that motivates the vertical/sexual-transmission questions for the related spirochete Borrelia.

title: Perinatal transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi: advancing scientific and clinical understanding of Lyme disease in pregnancy
authors: Banbury Center Lyme Disease in Pregnancy Working Group
key_findings: Reviews perinatal transmission of B. burgdorferi and argues for greater clinical and scientific attention to Lyme in pregnancy.
relevance_notes: Recent minority-leaning push to advance the congenital-transmission science.

title: Borrelia burgdorferi and autoimmune mechanisms: implications for mimicry, misdiagnosis, and mismanagement in Lyme disease and autoimmune disorders
key_findings: Reviews how Borrelia can mimic and possibly trigger autoimmune disease (including MS-like presentations), and the resulting misdiagnosis risk.
relevance_notes: Basis for the contested Lyme-MS mimicry/association invoked in familial-autoimmunity arguments.

title: Vaccination against Lyme disease with recombinant Borrelia burgdorferi outer-surface lipoprotein A with adjuvant
key_findings: Pivotal Phase III LYMErix (OspA) vaccine trial: ~76-80% reduction in new infections; transient arthralgia non-significantly increased; arthritis NOT increased versus placebo.
relevance_notes: Primary evidence on the only licensed human Lyme vaccine and its (non-)arthritis safety signal.

title: Identification of LFA-1 as a candidate autoantigen in treatment-resistant Lyme arthritis
key_findings: Proposed molecular mimicry between B. burgdorferi OspA and human LFA-1 in HLA-DRB1*0401 individuals as a mechanism for treatment-resistant Lyme arthritis; basis of the OspA-vaccine autoimmunity concern.
relevance_notes: The molecular-mimicry hypothesis (later not clinically confirmed) that drove fears about an OspA vaccine.

title: The Lyme vaccine: a cautionary tale
key_findings: LYMErix reduced infections ~80% yet was withdrawn within 3 years amid media coverage, side-effect fears, and falling sales rather than demonstrated harm.
relevance_notes: Mainstream account that the withdrawal was a risk-perception cascade, not proven vaccine harm.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Lyme Disease Vaccines: A Cautionary Tale for Risk Interventions in American Medicine and Public Health
key_findings: Despite safety/efficacy in trials and postmarketing surveillance, the Lyme vaccines were withdrawn amid litigation and risk perception; a sociological analysis of the collapse.
relevance_notes: Authoritative historical/sociological framing of why LYMErix failed.

title: The year that shaped the outcome of the OspA vaccine for human Lyme disease
key_findings: Reviews the 1998 FDA hearing and the OspA-LFA-1 molecular-mimicry concern, concluding the feared vaccine-induced autoimmunity was not borne out; informs next-generation design.
relevance_notes: Mainstream retrospective on the OspA-autoimmunity concern and its resolution.

title: Phase 3 VALOR Lyme Disease Trial (VLA15): primary vaccination series completion (Pfizer/Valneva)
key_findings: VLA15, a six-valent OspA-based Lyme vaccine engineered to avoid the LFA-1-homologous region, completed its Phase 3 VALOR primary series (9,437 participants) in 2024.
relevance_notes: Current OspA vaccine in development; signals the autoimmunity concern is considered manageable.

title: Immunological and Antigenic Signatures Associated with Chronic Illnesses after COVID-19 Vaccination (Yale LISTEN)
key_findings: Small cross-sectional study (42 PVS vs 22 controls) reporting altered T-cell profiles, EBV-reactivation serology, and circulating spike protein in post-vaccination-syndrome participants.
relevance_notes: Serious but preliminary, unreplicated, non-Lyme-specific PVS research; flagged speculative/preprint.

title: Investigation of Long COVID Prevalence and Its Relationship to Epstein-Barr Virus Reactivation
key_findings: Long-COVID symptoms were associated with serological evidence of EBV reactivation, illustrating that immune challenges can reactivate latent pathogens.
relevance_notes: Mainstream basis for the general 'immune event reactivates latent pathogen' mechanism (not Borrelia-specific).

title: Posttreatment Lyme disease syndrome
journal_or_publisher: Infectious Disease Clinics of North America
key_findings: Characterizes PTLDS as a real post-infectious syndrome; provides the chronic-illness substrate that non-specific immune activation can transiently flare.
relevance_notes: Anchors the immune-activation-flare and long-COVID/PTLDS-overlap framing.

title: Antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis is associated with HLA-DR molecules that bind a Borrelia burgdorferi peptide
key_findings: OspA-peptide-binding HLA-DR alleles mark antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis — the HLA/OspA axis underlying both the autoimmune-arthritis and vaccine-mimicry concerns.
relevance_notes: Mechanistic bridge to Topic 1 and to the OspA-vaccine autoimmunity hypothesis.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine Safety (CDC)
authors: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
journal_or_publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
key_findings: Summarizes the established safety profile of COVID-19 vaccines from large-scale surveillance; no established evidence of Borrelia reactivation.
relevance_notes: Vaccine-safety consensus anchor for the misinformation-sensitive claims.

title: Clinical, Epidemiologic, Histopathologic and Molecular Features of an Unexplained Dermopathy
key_findings: CDC study of 115 case-patients found no parasites/mycobacteria, fibers predominantly cellulose (cotton origin), and a clinical picture resembling delusional infestation; no infectious or environmental cause identified.
relevance_notes: Largest, most rigorous study; backbone of the mainstream position.

title: Delusional Infestation
key_findings: Comprehensive review of delusional infestation: fixed false belief of infestation, formication as a real sensory symptom, specimen sign, and antipsychotic treatment.
relevance_notes: Defines the diagnostic category most Morgellons cases are mapped onto.

title: Delusional Infestation, Including Delusions of Parasitosis: Results of Histologic Examination of Skin Biopsy and Patient-Provided Skin Specimens
key_findings: Patient-provided specimens consisted of cutaneous debris, environmental detritus, or textile/plant material; no objective evidence of infestation.
relevance_notes: Mainstream histologic basis for the textile-fiber interpretation.

title: Exploring the association between Morgellons disease and Lyme disease: identification of Borrelia burgdorferi in Morgellons disease patients
key_findings: Reports detection of B. burgdorferi in Morgellons skin specimens and argues for an association with Lyme disease.
relevance_notes: Core minority claim of a borrelial etiology; single-group, contested.

title: Morgellons disease: a filamentous borrelial dermatitis
key_findings: Frames Morgellons as a spirochetal dermatitis analogous to bovine digital dermatitis, with endogenous keratin/collagen filaments.
relevance_notes: Most developed statement of the borrelial-dermatitis hypothesis and the bovine analogy.

title: Characterization and evolution of dermal filaments from patients with Morgellons disease
key_findings: Reports Morgellons filaments are composed of keratin and collagen produced by keratinocytes/fibroblasts, not textile contaminants.
relevance_notes: Directly contradicts the cellulose finding; the central empirical dispute.

title: History of Morgellons disease: from delusion to definition
key_findings: Argues Morgellons was prematurely psychiatrized and proposes a case definition for an organic dermopathy.
relevance_notes: Minority framing/critique of the delusional-infestation consensus.

title: Morgellons disease: Analysis of a population with clinically confirmed microscopic subcutaneous fibers of unknown etiology
key_findings: Characterizes a self-selected Morgellons population reporting high rates of tick exposure, Lyme seropositivity, and systemic symptoms.
relevance_notes: Source of the demographic/symptom overlap claim; selection-biased cohort.

title: Association of spirochetal infection with Morgellons disease
key_findings: Reports spirochetes in Morgellons tissue and proposes a spirochetal etiology.
relevance_notes: Additional single-group spirochete-detection claim.

title: Characterization of Biofilm Formation by Borrelia burgdorferi In Vitro
key_findings: Reports in-vitro B. burgdorferi biofilm formation, invoked to explain persistence in Morgellons skin.
relevance_notes: Microbiology basis for biofilm-persistence claims applied to skin (unvalidated extension).

title: Morgellons disease: a review on current evidence and the need for consensus, standardized criteria, and future randomized controlled trials
key_findings: Recent review acknowledging heterogeneity, calling for standardized diagnostic criteria and controlled trials; notes lack of evidence for antibiotics.
relevance_notes: Shows mainstream concession that the category is heterogeneous and under-studied.

title: Neurologic Manifestations of Chronic Methamphetamine Abuse
key_findings: Reviews methamphetamine neurotoxicity and psychosis, including formication ('meth mites') as a frequent complaint in heavy users, driven by dopaminergic dysregulation.
relevance_notes: Mainstream basis for stimulant-induced formication and its mechanism.

title: Amphetamine-Induced Delusional Infestation
journal_or_publisher: American Journal of Psychiatry Residents' Journal
key_findings: Case discussion of delusional infestation precipitated by amphetamine use, illustrating the secondary (drug-induced) form.
relevance_notes: Directly documents amphetamine as a cause of the Morgellons-like infestation picture.

title: A Comparison of Methamphetamine-Induced Psychosis and Schizophrenia: A Review of Positive, Negative, and Cognitive Symptomatology
key_findings: Methamphetamine-induced psychosis shows disproportionately high tactile and visual hallucinations relative to schizophrenia; prevalence of stimulant psychosis ~26-46% in dependent users.
relevance_notes: Epidemiology and the prominence of tactile hallucinations in stimulant psychosis.

title: Delusional Infestation
key_findings: Distinguishes primary from secondary (drug/medical/psychiatric) delusional infestation; cocaine and amphetamines are recognized precipitants; antipsychotics treat it.
relevance_notes: Frames stimulant-induced DI as a secondary form and informs management.

title: Clinical, Epidemiologic, Histopathologic and Molecular Features of an Unexplained Dermopathy
key_findings: CDC Morgellons study noted detectable drugs in a notable share of the cohort alongside a delusional-infestation-like picture.
relevance_notes: The drug-detection signal linking Morgellons cohorts to substance use.

title: Morgellons disease: a filamentous borrelial dermatitis
key_findings: Argues Morgellons is an organic borrelial dermatitis, the competing explanation to stimulant-induced DI.
relevance_notes: Minority organic-etiology position that contests drug-attribution of all cases.

title: Lyme disease: a neuropsychiatric illness
key_findings: Foundational review cataloguing the neuropsychiatric manifestations of Lyme disease, including obsessions/compulsions among many psychiatric presentations.
relevance_notes: Classic anchor establishing the neuropsychiatric dimension of Lyme.

title: Late-stage neuropsychiatric Lyme borreliosis: differential diagnosis and treatment
key_findings: Reviews late neuropsychiatric Lyme presentations and their differential diagnosis and treatment.
relevance_notes: Clinical framing of neuropsychiatric Lyme.

title: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms in adults with Lyme disease
key_findings: Reports obsessive-compulsive symptomatology among adults with Lyme disease.
relevance_notes: One of few studies addressing OCD symptoms specifically in Lyme patients.

title: Neuropsychiatric Lyme Borreliosis: An Overview with a Focus on a Specialty Psychiatrist's Clinical Practice
key_findings: Argues tick-borne infection produces a spectrum of neuropsychiatric symptoms (including OCD-spectrum) via psychoimmunologic mechanisms.
relevance_notes: Primary minority/neuropsychiatric-Lyme position from a specialty psychiatrist.

title: Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal Infections (PANDAS): Clinical Description of the First 50 Cases
key_findings: Defines an infection-triggered autoimmune basal-ganglia syndrome producing acute-onset OCD and tics via molecular mimicry.
relevance_notes: The mechanistic template (PANDAS/PANS) that the Lyme-OCD hypothesis borrows.

title: Neuropsychiatric Manifestations and Cognitive Decline in Patients With Long-Standing Lyme Disease: A Scoping Review
key_findings: Scoping review of neuropsychiatric and cognitive findings in long-standing Lyme disease.
relevance_notes: Recent synthesis of the broader neuropsychiatric burden.

title: 2020 IDSA/AAN/ACR Lyme Disease Guidelines (neurologic Lyme sections)
key_findings: Defines diagnosis/treatment of neurologic Lyme (neuroborreliosis) and cautions against treating nonspecific symptoms as Lyme without objective evidence.
relevance_notes: Mainstream standard limiting antibiotic treatment to documented neuroborreliosis.

title: Case Report: PANDAS and Persistent Lyme Disease With Neuropsychiatric Symptoms: Treatment, Resolution, and Recovery
key_findings: Case of a child meeting PANDAS criteria with Lyme serology and neuropsychiatric symptoms (including obsessions/compulsions) reported to improve with treatment.
relevance_notes: Representative case-report evidence for the Lyme-triggered-PANS idea; hypothesis-generating only.

title: Concurrent Lyme disease and babesiosis: evidence for increased severity and duration of illness
key_findings: Co-infected patients had more symptoms and far longer illness (~50% symptomatic >=3 months vs ~4% with Lyme alone).
relevance_notes: Landmark evidence that Babesia co-infection worsens and prolongs Lyme illness.

title: Babesia microti-Borrelia burgdorferi Coinfection
key_findings: Reviews shared-vector co-transmission; ~20% of Lyme patients report concurrent babesiosis and up to ~25% of babesiosis patients have Lyme in endemic areas.
relevance_notes: Synthesis of co-infection epidemiology and biology.

title: Investigating disease severity in an animal model of concurrent babesiosis and Lyme disease
key_findings: Animal model shows altered immune responses and increased severity in concurrent Babesia/Borrelia infection.
relevance_notes: Mechanistic support for co-infection synergy.

title: Beyond Human Babesiosis: Prevalence and Association of Babesia Coinfection with Mortality in the United States, 2015-2022
key_findings: Large retrospective cohort associating Babesia coinfection with worse outcomes including mortality signals.
relevance_notes: Recent population-scale evidence on coinfection burden.

title: Coinfection by Ixodes tick-borne pathogens: ecological, epidemiological, and clinical consequences
key_findings: Reviews ecology and clinical consequences of Ixodes-borne co-infections including Babesia.
relevance_notes: Authoritative co-infection ecology/clinical review.

title: Empirical validation of the Horowitz Multiple Systemic Infectious Disease Syndrome Questionnaire for suspected Lyme disease
key_findings: Validation study of a questionnaire operationalizing the MSIDS multi-co-infection model of chronic Lyme.
relevance_notes: Primary minority/MSIDS source; co-infections real, treatment breadth contested.

title: Protomyxzoa rheumatica / FL1953 (novel protozoan claim, Fry Laboratories)
journal_or_publisher: Conference presentations / commercial laboratory (no robust peer-reviewed validation)
key_findings: Claims of a novel protozoan parasite (FL1953 / 'Protomyxzoa rheumatica') in chronic-illness patients, promoted with associated commercial testing and antiparasitic treatment.
relevance_notes: Flagged fringe/speculative: the linked PubMed Central search documents the near-absence of independent peer-reviewed validation; commercial conflict of interest. Included to record the claim honestly, not to endorse it.

title: Suicide and Lyme and associated diseases
key_findings: Argues infection-driven pro-inflammatory cytokines, inflammatory-metabolic changes, and quinolinic-acid/glutamate alterations increase suicidality, and that similar pathophysiology operates in Lyme and associated diseases.
relevance_notes: Primary minority source proposing an infection-specific suicide contribution; mechanism mainstream, magnitude/attribution contested.

title: Suicidal and homicidal tendencies after Lyme disease: an ignored problem
key_findings: Extends the neuropsychiatric-Lyme thesis to suicidal and aggressive/externalizing behavior.
relevance_notes: More speculative behavioral extension; flagged to avoid sensationalism, included for completeness.

title: Lyme neuroborreliosis presenting with alexithymia and suicide attempts
key_findings: Documents a neuroborreliosis case with suicidality that improved with treatment of the infection.
relevance_notes: Case-level evidence that active CNS infection can produce reversible suicidality.

title: Role of inflammation in suicide: from mechanisms to treatment
key_findings: Reviews inflammation and the kynurenine pathway in suicidality, including quinolinic acid as an NMDA agonist/excitotoxin.
relevance_notes: Mainstream mechanistic backbone any infection-suicide hypothesis relies on.

title: Connecting inflammation with glutamate agonism in suicidality (CSF quinolinic acid in suicide attempters)
key_findings: Found elevated CSF quinolinic acid in suicide attempters, linking inflammation to glutamatergic excitotoxicity in suicidality.
relevance_notes: Direct human evidence for the quinolinic-acid/suicide link invoked by the Lyme hypothesis.

title: Epidemiology of Suicide and the Psychiatric Perspective
journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
key_findings: Reviews suicide epidemiology and risk factors, including chronic illness, pain, and psychosocial stressors.
relevance_notes: Mainstream basis for the chronic-illness/invalidation suicide-risk pathway.

title: Concurrent Lyme disease and babesiosis: evidence for increased severity and duration of illness
key_findings: Co-infection increases severity and duration of illness, amplifying chronic-illness burden.
relevance_notes: Links the parasitic co-infection element of this topic to elevated illness burden.

title: Cross-reactivity in serological tests for Lyme disease and other spirochetal infections
key_findings: Documents antibody cross-reactivity among Borrelia, Treponema, and other spirochetes in serologic assays.
relevance_notes: Foundational evidence for Lyme/syphilis serologic cross-reactivity.

title: Evaluation of the fluorescent treponemal antibody-absorption (FTA-Abs) test specificity
key_findings: Lyme borreliosis is an important cause of false-positive FTA-Abs reactions; isolated positive FTA-Abs found in a large fraction of Lyme sera.
relevance_notes: Quantifies false-positive syphilis serology caused by Lyme.

title: Antibody Cross-Reactivity in Serodiagnosis of Lyme Disease
key_findings: Reviews cross-reactivity in Lyme serology caused by bacterial (relapsing-fever Borrelia, Treponema) and viral (EBV, CMV) infections.
relevance_notes: Modern synthesis of the cross-reactivity problem.

title: Borrelia burgdorferi in the nervous system: the new 'great imitator'
journal_or_publisher: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
key_findings: Frames neuroborreliosis as the new great imitator by explicit analogy to neurosyphilis.
relevance_notes: Origin of the Lyme-as-great-imitator framing central to this topic.

title: Neurosyphilis: The Great Imitator
key_findings: Reviews neurosyphilis as the original great imitator with staged spirochetal CNS disease and psychiatric manifestations.
relevance_notes: The syphilis template the Lyme parallel is built on.

title: Atypical Lyme borreliosis in an HIV-infected man
key_findings: HIV co-infected Lyme case with persistent erythema migrans, meningoradiculitis, and discordant serology (IFA negative, ELISA/Western blot positive); notes open question whether HIV alters Lyme course like it alters syphilis.
relevance_notes: Anchors the HIV-Lyme serology/course intersection.

title: Babesiosis as a cause of false-positive HIV serology
key_findings: Tick-borne babesiosis can produce false-positive HIV serology, illustrating cross-assay reverberation of tick-borne infections.
relevance_notes: Connects the parasitic co-infection (Topic 5) to HIV serology confounding.

title: Plaques of Alzheimer's disease originate from cysts of Borrelia burgdorferi, the Lyme disease spirochete
key_findings: Hypothesizes Borrelia cystic forms contribute to Alzheimer's plaques, modeled on syphilitic general paresis.
relevance_notes: Fringe extension of the spirochete-to-dementia template; hypothesis-level, under-replicated.

title: The Brilliance of Borrelia: Mechanisms of Host Immune Evasion by Lyme Disease-Causing Spirochetes
key_findings: Reviews Borrelia immune-evasion strategies: antigenic variation, complement evasion, lymph-node occupation, dysregulated B-cell proliferation, and humoral suppression.
relevance_notes: Overview of how Borrelia perturbs the immune/lymphocyte compartment.

title: Suppression of Long-Lived Humoral Immunity Following Borrelia burgdorferi Infection
key_findings: Borrelia induces abnormal, short-lived germinal centers that fail to generate durable memory B cells/plasma cells, broadly suppressing humoral immunity and leaving hosts susceptible to reinfection.
relevance_notes: Key mechanism: Borrelia-induced humoral immune suppression.

title: Suppression of host humoral immunity by Borrelia burgdorferi varies over the course of infection
key_findings: Characterizes how Borrelia-induced humoral suppression changes across the infection course.
relevance_notes: Recent refinement of the humoral-suppression mechanism.

title: Infection by Borrelia burgdorferi and cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
key_findings: Associates primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma with chronic Borrelia antigenic stimulation of cutaneous lymphoid tissue.
relevance_notes: Foundational paper linking infection-driven B-cell lymphoproliferation to Borrelia (a defined WBC disorder).

title: Eradication of Borrelia burgdorferi infection in primary marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of the skin
key_findings: Antibiotic eradication of Borrelia accompanied regression of cutaneous marginal-zone lymphoma, supporting a causal antigen-driven role.
relevance_notes: Infection->lymphoma->antibiotic-reversal chain, analogous to H. pylori MALT lymphoma.

title: Decreased CD57 lymphocyte subset in patients with chronic Lyme disease
key_findings: Reports decreased CD57+ NK-cell subset in 'chronic Lyme disease,' proposed as a biomarker.
relevance_notes: Primary minority biomarker claim; not validated as a clinical chronic-Lyme test by mainstream immunology.

title: CD4+ T-cell depletion in HIV infection: mechanisms of immunological failure
key_findings: Reviews mechanisms of CD4+ T-cell depletion (direct cytopathicity, immune activation, pyroptosis, lymphoid destruction) underlying HIV immunodeficiency.
relevance_notes: The archetypal WBC-disruption mechanism for comparison.

title: Borrelia burgdorferi Manipulates Innate and Adaptive Immunity to Establish Persistence in Rodent Reservoir Hosts
key_findings: Describes Borrelia manipulation of innate and adaptive immunity enabling persistence, including immunomodulation relevant to co-infection.
relevance_notes: Mechanistic basis for Borrelia-driven immune modulation and co-infection synergy.

title: New insights into the Tyrolean Iceman's origin and phenotype as inferred by whole-genome sequencing
key_findings: Whole-genome sequencing of the ~5,300-year-old Tyrolean Iceman recovered roughly two-thirds of a B. burgdorferi genome, the earliest documented human Lyme infection.
relevance_notes: Direct evidence that Borrelia long predates modern bioweapons; refutes 'man-made organism.'

title: Spirochete-like cells in a Dominican amber Amblyomma tick (Arachnida: Ixodidae)
key_findings: Reports Borrelia-like spirochetes in 15-20-million-year-old amber ticks, indicating Lyme-group bacteria predate humanity.
relevance_notes: Deep-time evidence that the organism is natural and ancient.

title: Bitten: The Secret History of Lyme Disease and Biological Weapons
key_findings: Documents Willy Burgdorfer's classified tick-borne bioweapon work and archival materials; argues (speculatively) for a possible link between weaponization research and the Lyme epidemic.
relevance_notes: Real investigative archival work; the documented history is solid, the epidemic-link conclusion is contested/speculative.

title: 2019 House amendment (Rep. Christopher Smith) directing DoD Inspector General review of tick weaponization, 1950-1975 (FY2020 NDAA)
journal_or_publisher: US Congress / Defense Authorization Act FY2020
key_findings: House passed an amendment requiring the DoD IG to review whether the military experimented with weaponizing disease-carrying ticks and whether any were released.
relevance_notes: Documented legislative event; a request to investigate, not a finding.

title: Did Lawmakers Demand the Pentagon Disclose If It Developed Weaponized Ticks? (fact-check)
key_findings: Confirms the amendment is real while rating the broader 'Lyme as engineered epidemic' claim as unsupported.
relevance_notes: Balanced fact-check separating documented event from speculative conclusion.

title: House measure on weaponized ticks revives discredited conspiracy theory
key_findings: Journalistic context characterizing the bioweapon-origin theory as discredited while reporting the legislative action.
relevance_notes: Mainstream journalistic framing.

title: Lab 257: The Disturbing Story of the Government's Secret Plum Island Germ Laboratory
key_findings: Chronicles Plum Island secrecy and raises the proximity-based suspicion of a Lyme connection; Plum Island's documented work was on livestock diseases.
relevance_notes: Source of the Plum Island narrative; proximity-and-secrecy reasoning, not evidence of Lyme origin.

title: Troublesome Ticks: Dispelling Bioweapon Rumors
key_findings: Infectious-disease commentary explaining the natural ecology of the Lyme epidemic and refuting the bioweapon-origin claim while acknowledging historical research.
relevance_notes: Mainstream ID framing and ecological explanation.
